title: Functional atlas of vertebrate viral RNA elements that stabilize RNA and enhance translation.
journal: Cell, 2026 Aug (online 2026-08-13), PMID 42594865, pii S0092-8674(26)00870-6. Europe PMC: isOpenAccess=N, inPMC=N, no PMCID, hasSuppl=N, fullTextUrl availability 'Subscription required'.
data_url: Only public deposit found: PRIDE PXD071193 (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/pride/archive/projects/PXD071193), licence CC0, published 2026-06-21. No GEO/SRA/BioProject/Zenodo/figshare/DataCite record for the MPRA data was found.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC core record (no PMCID, no supplementary files endpoint, no accession annotations). NCBI elink pubmed->gds/bioproject/sra for PMID 42594865: zero linked records. GEO (db=gds) searches for 'Kim VN[Author]', 'Seo JJ[Author]', 'TENT4', 'mixed tailing', 'Potamipivirus', 'virome', 'massively parallel reporter assay AND virus' (2026 dates): no series matching this study; the only TENT4 hit is GSE293395 (2025 HAV nanopore). BioProject searches: only PRJNA611047 (2020 fCLIP-seq) and unrelated 2026 entries. DataCite title query returned 0. Zenodo query returned 2 unrelated records. GitHub API: 0 repos for 'viral RNA element MPRA' or 'mixed tailing TENT4'. PRIDE v3 API: project metadata read in full, and the file list enumerated - exactly 3 files (Q20_scr_TMT6plex_Eclipse_240913.raw 783 MB, txt_Q20scr.zip 29.6 MB MaxQuant search output, mqpar.xml 28 kB).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the MPRA itself: ~200,000 genomic segments from 297 vertebrate-infecting viral genera, elements in 18-19 genera grouped into six subclasses, TENT4-dependent vs independent classes, Pt1/Potamipivirus. That is the abstract (plus the identical PRIDE project description); the full text, the data availability statement and the supplementary tables are behind the paywall and not in PMC, so I could not see any file, column, unit or row count for the sequence->score table.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL (checked). No public deposit of the MPRA sequence->score data could be located in GEO, SRA, BioProject, Zenodo, figshare, DataCite or GitHub, and PubMed elink returns no linked datasets. The article is not open access and has no PMCID, so even the data availability statement is unreadable without publisher access (CLAUDE.md forbids scraping the publisher site). The one public deposit, PRIDE PXD071193, is a single TMT-6plex RNA-bait pulldown: one 783 MB raw file plus a MaxQuant txt zip - raw mass spec, excluded by project rules, and unrelated to the 200k-segment assay.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not verified (stopped at A1). An MPRA would plausibly yield a per-segment stability and translation score as a column, but no table was seen, so whether scores are per-segment-per-replicate, per-element, or only as called hits is unknown.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not verified (stopped at A1). Library designs usually ship the oligo sequence, but it is equally common for Cell supplements to list only viral genome coordinates and genus, which would require reconstructing ~200k segment sequences from 297 viral reference genomes.

a4_units_stated.note: Not verified (stopped at A1). MPRA outputs are typically log2 RNA/DNA or RNA/input ratios; normalization scheme, replicate structure and whether TENT4-knockout/RG7834 arms are on a common scale are all unknown.

a5_enough_rows.note: Not verified. The abstract claims ~200,000 segments, which would comfortably exceed the 1,500-row bar, but I saw no file and no count. Note the effective unit may be the element or the viral genus (297), not the segment, since tiled overlapping segments are highly correlated.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: Unknown; a 200k-row x (sequence + few score columns) table would be well under 100 MB.
a6_fits_laptop.note: The only plausible failure here would be if just the raw FASTQ were released, in which case the working set is sequencing-scale and the project is out of scope under CLAUDE.md.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not verified (stopped at A1). Already one inconsistency between the two author-written descriptions I did retrieve: the Cell abstract says the stabilizing elements are distributed across 19 genera, the PRIDE project description (same text) says 18.

a8_label_provenance.note: Likely fine on principle, unverified in files: the label would be a measured reporter readout (RNA abundance / translation from a pooled assay), not another model's output, and not computable from the sequence features. The risk is subtler - 'subclass' assignments are the authors' clustering of their own data and would be a leaky target, whereas the continuous stability score would not.

existing_models.name: Saluki (Agarwal & Kelley, Genome Biology 2022, 10.1186/s13059-022-02811-x, PMC9684954)
existing_models.score_and_split: Hybrid CNN+RNN predicting mRNA half-life from sequence plus coding frame and splice-site tracks; abstract reports r=0.77. The split type is not stated in the abstract I retrieved and I did not open the full text.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Abstract names pervasive technical noise and measurement bias across the 39 human / 27 mouse decay datasets as the problem they had to correct for; I did not read their discussion.

existing_models.name: mRNABench (Shi et al., bioRxiv 2025, 10.1101/2025.07.05.662870, PPR1047706)
existing_models.score_and_split: Benchmark, not a single model: 10 curated datasets, 59 tasks (half-life, localization, translation efficiency), 18 families of nucleotide foundation models, 135k experiments comparing frozen-embedding representational quality.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Abstract frames the gap as the dearth and homogeneity of standardized mature-mRNA benchmarks; viral elements are not among the ten datasets as far as the abstract indicates.

existing_models.name: Bacterial synthetic-mRNA stability model (Nature Communications 2024, 10.1038/s41467-024-54059-7, PMC11541907)
existing_models.score_and_split: Biophysical + ML sequence-to-function model fit to massively parallel kinetic decay measurements on >50,000 bacterial mRNAs (half-lives ~20 s to ~20 min); the abstract gives no held-out metric.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Abstract states that predicting stability from sequence remains hard because of coupled interactions (translation, secondary structure, G-quadruplexes, RppH).

backbone.name: RNA-FM, or an mRNABench-style frozen nucleotide LM (Nucleotide Transformer / HyenaDNA) for 150-300 nt segments
backbone.hardware: CPU, if the segments are a few hundred nt and number ~200k; embeddings cacheable once. Not assessed against real file sizes.
backbone.licence: RNA-FM code MIT on GitHub (not re-checked this session). The dataset licence is unknown because no dataset was found; the PRIDE mass-spec deposit is CC0.

integration.partner_dataset: Not scored (stopped at A1). The natural partners would be NCBI Virus / RefSeq viral genomes on taxonomy ID plus genome coordinates, and host mRNA half-life compendia (Saluki's 39 human datasets).
integration.join_key: Viral taxonomy ID + genome accession + segment coordinates (none of which I could confirm are present).
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Not written: the data to join does not exist publicly as far as I could verify.

controls.positive_control: Not assessed. The obvious one would be that the model recovers the paper's own TENT4-dependent subclasses as high-stability outliers, plus a trivial target such as GC content or segment length from sequence.
controls.negative_control: Not assessed. Label shuffling, and shuffling within viral genus to test that grouped CV actually groups tiled overlapping segments.
controls.external_validation: Not assessed. In principle a held-out-genus split and the TENT4-knockout / RG7834 arm would serve, if those arms are released as separate columns.

honest_claim_h3: Cannot be written against verified data. The best available version would be: 'from sequence alone, predicts the reporter stability score of a tiled viral genome segment, among segments from the 297 vertebrate-infecting genera this group chose to tile, measured in one cell line under one construct' - which is a statement about one assay context, not about viral regulation generally.
ml_idea: Frozen RNA-FM embeddings of each ~150-300 nt viral segment plus a small regression head predicting the measured stability and translation scores, evaluated on held-out viral genera, with the transfer question 'does a model fitted on TENT4-dependent elements generalize to the TENT4-independent ones?' This is parked, not rejected on merit: the task shape is good, but no sequence->score table is publicly retrievable today.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Open the data availability statement and Table S1 (needs institutional access to cell.com, or wait for a PMC deposit) and check two things: does a GEO/Zenodo accession exist, and does the table carry the segment nucleotide sequence rather than only viral genome coordinates. If it is coordinates only, add a day of genome-fetching per 297 genera before any modelling.

verdict_reason: A1 fails as of 2026-10-05: the only public deposit is a single raw TMT mass-spec run in PRIDE (PXD071193), the MPRA data has no findable GEO/SRA/Zenodo/DataCite record, PubMed elink returns nothing, and the paywalled full text puts the data availability statement itself out of reach. Nothing in Part A beyond A1 could be verified in files. The underlying task (sequence -> measured RNA stability over ~200k segments, with RNA-FM as a frozen backbone and held-out-genus splits) is attractive enough to re-check in a few months for a released accession; until then there is no data to model.
